text: Nell had only meant to look around the old lighthouse, not take anything. It had been empty for forty years, and the door creaked like an old ship. That night, back home, she put it in her sock drawer. Then she took it out and put it under her mattress. Then she moved it to a shoebox at the back of the wardrobe, as far from her bed as it could possibly go. She couldn't stop picturing the empty nail. Every time the wind rattled the window, she glanced at the wardrobe. At dinner, when Dad mentioned that the lighthouse was being turned into a museum, Nell knocked over her glass of water. 'Have you been up there?' he asked. 'No,' she said, and immediately felt her face go hot. She lay awake until two in the morning, staring at the wardrobe door. The next afternoon, she rode her bike all the way back to the lighthouse, hung the key back on its nail, and left a note underneath that said, in very small writing, 'Sorry. I won't do it again.'
